definition.message:
{{#is_alert}}
## What's happening?

Power sensor **{{sensor.name}}** in slot {{slot.name}} on firewall **{{device_ip.name}}** is in alarm.
{{/is_alert}}

{{#is_recovery}}
## Recovered

Power sensor {{sensor.name}} in slot {{slot.name}} on firewall {{device_ip.name}} is no longer in alarm.
{{/is_recovery}}

{{^is_recovery}}

---

## Impact

An unstable power supply can cause the firewall to reboot or shut down.

---

## Why?

Possible causes:
* **A failing power supply.**
* **An unstable or lost power feed.**

---

## How to troubleshoot and resolve the issue?

1. Run `show system environmentals` on the firewall to see the sensor's reading and thresholds.
2. Check the power supply and its feed.
3. Replace the power supply if the alarm persists.

---

## Related links

* [Documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/pan_firewall/)
* [Metrics Explorer](/metric/explorer?exp_metric=pan_firewall.power.voltage&exp_scope=device_ip:{{device_ip.name}},sensor:{{sensor.name}}&exp_agg=max&exp_type=line)
{{/is_recovery}}
definition.name: [Palo Alto Networks Firewall] Power sensor {{sensor.name}} is in alarm on {{device_ip.name}}

description: Tracks whether PAN-OS reports any power sensor on the firewall in alarm, usually because its voltage is above its maximum or below its minimum. A power alarm points to a failing power supply or an unstable feed that can take the device down.
title: Power sensor is in alarm
